Centurion Builder

By: Eugene Botha | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
....a builder scamming people out of millions

Unique Selling Point:
This is in the public interest to expose this charlatan.

Further information:
Ian Bann of Heksagon Construction (previously Homeostasus Construction) operates mainly in the Centurion area in Pretoria and has been scamming people out of large amounts of money for a number of years. He appears very professional, send quotes on time and reasonable and always pitches up in time with a team to start the work. It seems he s very good at digging foundations and sometimes building walls, but that is where everything stops. Then it is excuses, labour problems, need for more money, and more lies.

I was contacted by a Yolandi and Kobus van den Berg who has paid Ian Bann a total of R340 901.08 and all they have to show for it is a few trenches and half a wall. And they are far from the only ones!!! We have 5 more case studies where Bann has taken hundreds of thousands of rands from people in the area.

This is what Yolandi and Kobus van den Berg say:

"As discussed on Friday afternoon about Ian Bann...

Ian Bann presents himself well, very quick with response to quote, site visit and also able to start as quick as possible.
His website is very professional and indicates a lot of rewards achieved.

As with any building contractor he has a contract that he gives through that is indicative of his professionalism and everything in the contract makes you believe that he will ensure full compliance to the project, otherwise he will be subjected to the penalties in the contract.

He starts off on time, but there is from week one an indication that his people lives in areas that are heavily affected by strikes, transport constraints and cannot be on time.

What he can do is dig foundations, cast the foundation and start building the walls, but that is where it ends.
There is always a shortage of material, although the money for it has been paid – in some cases POP are submitted to the clients but the material never arrives. In some cases material, like paint is paid for, but the lowest quality is bought and not enough, workers sit and wait for the next tin, that can only be mixed by a certain person at the area where it is bought.
His “workmanship” stops at building wall. This is where the real time constraints start and the project gets delayed.
No electrical provisions are made for (i.e. conduits for electricity, plug points etc).
No drain work provision made for.

His preferred way of flat roofing is rib and block – which is left 1/3 into the work then he leaves site.
When a concrete roof slab is thrown there is no electrical boxes, piping or conduits, because his electrician is busy at another site, he jumps in and do it himself, but does not have a clue and afterward a new false sealing must be done, that is if the roof can be used.

Different day labourers each week and all are complaining that they are not paid…threatening the owners on site.

His kids are being used as an escape route, sick and unwell and needs be attended to, hence why he cannot attend to the sites.
He overruns on each project milestone and will always do something to make it up. He always promises that he will provide a project plan on how he will pull back to get on time, but just show up with a clip board and a piece of written paper.

His “bakkie” is always on a breakdown, and cannot do certain deliveries or get to site.

He uses the material of other sub-contractors and the owners of the property."

Apart from the van den Bergs, we will use 3 other case studies who have recently been scammed.

Modus Operandi:
Get interviews and cutaways with victims
Get Ian Bann to give a quote on work to be done and film it -- then we have him on camera.
Confront Bann about the work not completed

Various attorneys have been involved but so far without any success. However, Christoff Loch, an attorney who worked with Ian Bann to represent him in cases in the past, eventually saw through him and ended his services. Christoff indicated that he will be available in case more information is needed from him.

A typical example of a very smooth scammer who is raking in millions and defrauding people left, right and center. We have done a consumer trace on him and it seems that he is in debt review, so victims do not have achnace of getting money back.

Script:


Andre:
Personally I think he is a con artist. He is a liar and he is a thief.

V/O:
Andre Van Schalkwyk, a Centurion homeowner, is speaking about a building contractor who he says scammed him out of hundreds of thousands of rands.

The building contractor, Ian Bann, is the sole owner and director of Hexsagon Construction, a company that operates mainly in Centurion, Pretoria. He was contracted in February to construct a covered patio and braai area, and informed van Schalkwyk that it would take only six to eight weeks. However, progress was excruciatingly slow.
10



LINK:
Van Schalkwyk became increasingly agitated and after many months of frustration things came to head. 5
Andre:
So one Friday morning I phoned and I said to him about half past nine, quarter to ninein the morning. I said “Where’s you people? It is nine o’clock. You are not on my site, when are you going to pitch up?” And he said to me,”OK Andre, I think that’s it. I have had enough of you. He told me he is not coming back.
V/O:
So, Bann simply abandoned the project after 16 weeks, in the middle of June.

Van Schalkwyk had to pay another contractor to complete the work, in addition to the two hundred and sixty thousand Rand he had already paid to Bann.
5

18
Andre:
Something that should have been roundabout three hundred and fifty thousand, maybe four hundred thousand is turning at a million. I want to cry. I promise you, I want to sit in a corner and cry.
LINK:
Van Schalkwyk is but one of a number of people who contacted Carte Blanche about Hexsagon and Ian Bann who is active in the Centurion area. They all say he has swindled them out of significant amounts of money.
13
V/O:
Nicho Le Roux engaged Bann in November 2019 to construct a patio next to his house and paid him a deposit of forty thousand rand. And then nothing happened.
23
Nicho:
Come January I start reaching out to him. I start asking him where is the building plans, where is the project plans, It took him eight months to get me a project plan. Eight months.
V/O:
Le Roux says Bann finally commenced the work in September 2020, and abandoned the project two months later, in November. In total Le Roux says he has paid Bann more that one hundred and ten thousand rand. After Baan left, Le Roux made a disturbing discovery. 17
Nicho:
All the monies that I paid to him for services, for rubbish removal, for plans approval, for the engineer. All the monies I paid over to him, he never paid over to them.
V/O:
Kobus and Yolandi van den Berg wanted an extension to their main bedroom, a deck around their pool and an enclosed braai area. They paid Bann three hundred and forty thousand rand in February. 22
Kobus:
From the start of the project should actually have taken him 8 weeks, that is what his time schedule was to finish off the project. And 8 weeks down line in April, when we came back from holiday, he was not even thirty percent done with everything.
V/O:
Van den Berg says that there were many more delays and sloppy work that had to be corrected. In May Bann said he needed more money to pay for the material for the deck around the pool.
11
Kobus:
I paid the money directly to him. The money was never paid into the company, so the decking never arrived.
V/O:
In June Bann informed Van den Berg that he is not willing to complete the project.
9
Kobus:
He basically quit. He decided that he was not going to finish the project. It was not me telling him we had to part ways.
V/O:
Bann promised to refund the Van den Bergs some of the money, and even handed them a settlement agreement.
5
LINK:
This is the settlement agreement offered to Van den Berg in which Bann undertook to refund R225 000 in three instalments.
V/O:
The first instalment was due on the 6th of August. To date the van den Berg’s have not received a cent.

But, why did these complainants choose to contact Bann in the first place? They all say it was because his website attracted their attention.
Kobus:
It is one of the most professional sites I have seen, websites
Nicho:
The references on the website also indicates a lot of rewards, building rewards of the previous year, as well as accolades from apparent customers. That is what made one make this decision.
Andre:
At that stage I did go to Hallo Peter, and I did a search on Hallo Peter, and I picked up nothing.
V/O:
And they all say their initial interactions with Bann himself was quite positive. 4
Nico:
I called Hexsagon and I asked for a site visit to discuss. He came very quickly. That impressed me. Very professional in the way he approached.
Kobus:
He was the quickest to get back with a quote. He was very punctual. He had all of his contracts and everything in place.
V/O:
Based on these positive exchanges with Bann, they engaged his services.

We also requested a quotation from Bann to replace this old wooden deck with a concrete slab and to build a room on top of it. . He arrived punctually, offered a one-stop in-house solution, including all services and negotiations with stakeholders. He appeared quite knowledgeable about building plans. 18
Ian:
In die ou dae, 15 jaar terug kon jy net bouplanne ingedien het vir jou stoep en dit ingedien het en net die bestaande planne aangehg het. Nou sê die munisipaliteit jy moet die hele huis aandui., en dit is waar die geneukery kom. Ons teken jou hele huis oor.
V/O:
He added that we would receive two quotes once he gets back to his computer: one for the construction and one for the plans.
LINK:
The quotes we requested arrived in our inbox within 2 hours of his site visit. They are detailed and itemized and creates the impression of efficiency.
V/O:
And even formal building plans would be taken care of.
Ian:
Ek is ‘n plan tekenaar. Ek teken dit self. So ek gaan dit teken. Ek teken dit.
V/O:
This initial undercover interaction with Bann raised no red flags and it is understandable why people signed up with him.

However, the complainants all say that once deposits have been paid, things changed drastically. Progress is slow, unschooled day labourers are employed, and endless excuses are offered for the delays.
Nicho:
His laptop got stolen, then his phone was broken, then the bakkie that they used to transport their staff was broken, then he had issues with his kids at school.
Andre:
And he would come to you and say that there is a strike and his people can’t work.
V/O:
They eventually got fed up with the inefficiency and excuses and began putting pressure on him.
They say that is when he walked off site never to return.
A day after Bann abandoned his building site in June, van Schalkwyk recieved a telephone call from a stranger. 12
Andre:
And he said to me, “Do you know Ian Bann?” I said “Yes I know Ian Bann, he has done work for us, he’s actually left the site on Friday”. He said, “You’ve got to be careful with this man. He’s done the same thing to two people in Midstream, he walks off the site and takes their money and he just goes.
V/O:
Alarmed van Schalkwyk followed up and in July he made contact with Le Roux and Van den Berg, and a number of other Hexsagon complainants.
7
Nicho:
And the reason we came together as a group is Ok, we all suffered. How do we protect other people.
Andre:
Because if he is doing this to us, there is a good chance that he is also doing it to to somebody else as well.
V/O:
They agreed to report Hexsagon on Hello Peter and to contact Carte Blanche. We contacted Bann to get his side of the story, but he declined and on-camera interview. We sent him the allegations and he agreed to answer in writing, but did not stick to the deadline. We went to confront him where he was quoting for a new project.

We found him to the back yard.
Confrontation

Claire:
Hallo Mr Ian Bann, Claire fro Carte Blanche. How are you.

Bann:
Good and you?

Claire:
I am very well. I would like to know if you would agree to an on-camera interview, Mr Bann?

Bann:
I said no. You will have our response by this afternoon.

Claire:
You said this morning, Mr Bann. It is Wednesday morning. I sent you the questions. You should have the answers. Why wouldn’t answer the questions on why you won’t refund people that have paid you money, Mr Bann? I think people do deserve an answer…………Mr Bann, the people deserve their money back. The people deserve their money back, Mr Bann…. So, you will not answer the questions?

It is unbelievable. It is just unbelievable. Do you know what’s upsetting to me is that we contacted Mr Bann as Carte Blanche asking him to answer these questions, and after we contacted him, telling him that we know that he is taking money from people and not refunding them, he is still seeing new clients.
V/O:
Late in the afternoon, after the confrontation, Bann responded in writing to the allegations made against him.

• He denies that he uses unskilled day labourers. He says he has a fixed team, but because of Covid it is sometimes necessary to use other labourers.
• He rejects the allegation that he takes money and then doesn’t provide services.
• He denies that he stopped construction at the three premises in question and simply walked away. He says he made several attempts to arrive at a resolution with the homeowners.
• He grants that he did not honour the agreement to repay van den Berg but says there are other avenues of recourse open to van den Berg to resolve the issues.
• He says many unforeseen factors can cause legitimate delays on building projects.
• He denies that he has, at any stage, presented himself to clients as a qualified draughtsman.
• He concludes his letter by saying that he has never deliberately harmed or misguided consumers.

The complainants have all given up hope of getting a refund from either Hexsagon or Ian Bann, for any of the huge amounts they paid. However, they feel their small group does serve a purpose.

Claire:
What are you hoping to achive ultimately?

Andre:
I have to warn people. Stay away from this man. Don’t use him. He will steal your money.

We sent him the allegations and he agreed to answer in writing, but did not stick to the deadline. We went to confront him where he was quoting for a new project. We found him to the back yard. Confrontation Claire: Hallo Mr Ian Bann, Claire fro Carte Blanche. How are you. Bann: Good and you? Claire: I am very well. I would like to know if you would agree to an on-camera interview, Mr Bann? Bann: I said no. You will have our response by this afternoon. Claire: You said this morning, Mr Bann. It is Wednesday morning. I sent you the questions. You should have the answers. Why wouldn’t answer the questions on why you won’t refund people that have paid you money, Mr Bann? I think people do deserve an answer…………Mr Bann, the people deserve their money back. The people deserve their money back, Mr Bann…. So, you will not answer the questions? It is unbelievable. It is just unbelievable. Do you know what’s upsetting to me is that we contacted Mr Bann as Carte Blanche asking him to answer these questions, and after we contacted him, telling him that we know that he is taking money from people and not refunding them, he is still seeing new clients. V/O: Late in the afternoon, after the confrontation, Bann responded in writing to the allegations made against him. • He denies that he uses unskilled day labourers. He says he has a fixed team, but because of Covid it is sometimes necessary to use other labourers. • He rejects the allegation that he takes money and then doesn’t provide services. • He denies that he stopped construction at the three premises in question and simply walked away. He says he made several attempts to arrive at a resolution with the homeowners. • He grants that he did not honour the agreement to repay van den Berg but says there are other avenues of recourse open to van den Berg to resolve the issues. • He says many unforeseen factors can cause legitimate delays on building projects. • He denies that he has, at any stage, presented himself to clients as a qualified draughtsman. • He concludes his letter by saying that he has never deliberately harmed or misguided consumers. The complainants have all given up hope of getting a refund from either Hexsagon or Ian Bann, for any of the huge amounts they paid. However, they feel their small group does serve a purpose. Claire: What are you hoping to achive ultimately? Andre: I have to warn people. Stay away from this man. Don’t use him. He will steal your money.

metadata.Further information: Ian Bann of Heksagon Construction (previously Homeostasus Construction) operates mainly in the Centurion area in Pretoria and has been scamming people out of large amounts of money for a number of years. He appears very professional, send quotes on time and reasonable and always pitches up in time with a team to start the work. It seems he s very good at digging foundations and sometimes building walls, but that is where everything stops. Then it is excuses, labour problems, need for more money, and more lies. I was contacted by a Yolandi and Kobus van den Berg who has paid Ian Bann a total of R340 901.08 and all they have to show for it is a few trenches and half a wall. And they are far from the only ones!!! We have 5 more case studies where Bann has taken hundreds of thousands of rands from people in the area. This is what Yolandi and Kobus van den Berg say: "As discussed on Friday afternoon about Ian Bann... Ian Bann presents himself well, very quick with response to quote, site visit and also able to start as quick as possible. His website is very professional and indicates a lot of rewards achieved. As with any building contractor he has a contract that he gives through that is indicative of his professionalism and everything in the contract makes you believe that he will ensure full compliance to the project, otherwise he will be subjected to the penalties in the contract. He starts off on time, but there is from week one an indication that his people lives in areas that are heavily affected by strikes, transport constraints and cannot be on time. What he can do is dig foundations, cast the foundation and start building the walls, but that is where it ends. There is always a shortage of material, although the money for it has been paid – in some cases POP are submitted to the clients but the material never arrives. In some cases material, like paint is paid for, but the lowest quality is bought and not enough, workers sit and wait for the next tin, that can only be mixed by a certain person at the area where it is bought. His “workmanship” stops at building wall. This is where the real time constraints start and the project gets delayed. No electrical provisions are made for (i.e. conduits for electricity, plug points etc). No drain work provision made for. His preferred way of flat roofing is rib and block – which is left 1/3 into the work then he leaves site. When a concrete roof slab is thrown there is no electrical boxes, piping or conduits, because his electrician is busy at another site, he jumps in and do it himself, but does not have a clue and afterward a new false sealing must be done, that is if the roof can be used. Different day labourers each week and all are complaining that they are not paid…threatening the owners on site. His kids are being used as an escape route, sick and unwell and needs be attended to, hence why he cannot attend to the sites. He overruns on each project milestone and will always do something to make it up. He always promises that he will provide a project plan on how he will pull back to get on time, but just show up with a clip board and a piece of written paper. His “bakkie” is always on a breakdown, and cannot do certain deliveries or get to site. He uses the material of other sub-contractors and the owners of the property." Apart from the van den Bergs, we will use 3 other case studies who have recently been scammed. Modus Operandi: Get interviews and cutaways with victims Get Ian Bann to give a quote on work to be done and film it -- then we have him on camera. Confront Bann about the work not completed Various attorneys have been involved but so far without any success. However, Christoff Loch, an attorney who worked with Ian Bann to represent him in cases in the past, eventually saw through him and ended his services. Christoff indicated that he will be available in case more information is needed from him. A typical example of a very smooth scammer who is raking in millions and defrauding people left, right and center. We have done a consumer trace on him and it seems that he is in debt review, so victims do not have achnace of getting money back.
